output.answer:
**Question:** wells fargo nim
*As of 2026-10-03*

**Interpreted as:** 'wells fargo' read as Wells Fargo & Company (WFC), the SEC registrant; fiscal year = calendar year. No period given: latest reported period is Q2 FY2026 (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30), reported 2026-07-14; Q3 FY2026 ended 2026-09-30 but results are not yet released. 'nim' read as net interest margin on the taxable-equivalent basis Wells Fargo reports, plus net interest income for context. Comparison read as sequential (Q1 FY2026) and year-over-year (Q2 FY2025) change in NIM.

| | Net interest margin, taxable-equivalent basis (%) | Net interest income (USD millions) |
|---|---|---|
| Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) | 2.43 [1][2] | 12,317 [1][3] |
| Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) | 2.47 [1][4] | 12,096 [1][5] |
| Q2 FY2025 (quarter ended June 30, 2025) | 2.68 [1][6] | 11,708 [1][3] |

- Wells Fargo's net interest margin (NIM) on a taxable-equivalent basis was 2.43% for Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026), as reported in the company's July 14, 2026 earnings release. [1][2][6]
- Wells Fargo's net interest income was $12,317 million in Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026), up 2% from Q1 FY2026 and up 5% from Q2 FY2025. [1][7]
- NIM on a taxable-equivalent basis fell 4 basis points sequentially, from 2.47% in Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) to 2.43% in Q2 FY2026, a change the company attributed to growth in interest-bearing deposits and continued growth in its Markets business. [7][1]
- NIM on a taxable-equivalent basis fell 25 basis points year over year, from 2.68% in Q2 FY2025 (quarter ended June 30, 2025) to 2.43% in Q2 FY2026. [1][6]
- The Q2 FY2026 NIM is reported on a taxable-equivalent basis, which includes taxable-equivalent adjustments of $75 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, predominantly related to tax-exempt income on certain loans and securities, using a 21% federal statutory tax rate. [6][2]
- Wells Fargo does not issue formal NIM guidance; on the Q2 FY2026 earnings call materials it guided only to 2026 net interest income of +/- $50 billion (with NII excluding Markets of +/- $48 billion and Markets NII of +/- $2 billion), unchanged from prior guidance. [7][8]
- Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo said on September 15, 2026 that third-quarter net interest margin is expected to be better than the bank's initial expectation, while maintaining the full-year NII (~$50 billion) and expense (~$55.7 billion) forecasts, as reported by Reuters. [9]

**Not available**
- Net interest margin for Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026): Q3 FY2026 ended September 30, 2026 but results had not been released as of October 3, 2026; the latest reported NIM is Q2 FY2026 (2.43%). The company's Q2 FY2026 materials only give qualitative commentary that Q3 NIM is expected to be better than its initial expectation (Reuters, September 15, 2026), not a figure. [7][9]
- Company-issued NIM guidance or target for any future period: Wells Fargo does not publish a NIM guidance figure; its 2026 outlook table gives only net interest income guidance (+/- $50 billion) and qualitative commentary on NIM drivers. [7][8]
